paragraphs.paragraph: The future Redeemer will come from the house of Jesse, and the spirit of the Lord will grant him wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of God. He will judge justly, protect the poor, act through spiritual power, and draw his strength from righteousness and faithfulness.
paragraphs.title: The Redeemer and His Qualities

answers: The stem of Jesse
The house of Pharaoh
The family of Esau
easy.explanation: Isaiah 11:1 says, “There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse.”
easy.q: From whose stem will the rod described in the passage come?

answers: The spirit of war
The spirit of the Lord
The spirit of the sea
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.”
easy.q: What shall rest upon the Redeemer?

answers: Kings only
Armies only
The poor
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “With righteousness shall he judge the poor.”
easy.q: Whom will the Redeemer judge with righteousness?

answers: Wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the Lord
Riches, trade, building, and farming
Speed, height, strength, and fame
medium.explanation: These qualities are listed in Isaiah 11:2.
medium.q: Which list correctly names the qualities given to the Redeemer?

answers: Because he cannot see or hear
Because his judgment is based on righteousness and the fear of the Lord
Because he gives every judgment to other rulers
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts ordinary outward judgment with his righteous and discerning judgment.
medium.q: Why will the Redeemer not judge merely by the sight of his eyes or the hearing of his ears?

answers: Righteousness will be a sign of strength and readiness
Righteousness will keep him from acting
Righteousness will be merely decorative
medium.explanation: A girdle was worn around the body, so the image presents righteousness as part of his strength and readiness.
medium.q: What does the word “girdle” suggest in the phrase “righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins”?

answers: He will have no connection with the past
He will be connected to Jesse’s line while bringing new growth
He will mainly be a farmer
challenge.explanation: The image joins the Redeemer to Jesse’s roots while emphasizing new life and growth.
challenge.q: What does the image of a rod growing from Jesse’s stem teach about the Redeemer?

answers: Wisdom and the fear of the Lord lead him to judge fairly and defend the weak
Might causes him to avoid judgment entirely
Knowledge causes him to judge only by outward appearance
challenge.explanation: His spiritual qualities are shown through righteous judgment and care for the poor and meek.
challenge.q: How are the Redeemer’s qualities connected with his leadership?

answers: Faithfulness is unrelated to his rule
Faithfulness is a central source of his stability and strength
Faithfulness prevents him from taking action
challenge.explanation: The verse presents faithfulness as something that firmly surrounds and strengthens him.
challenge.q: What does “faithfulness the girdle of his reins” indicate about the Redeemer?

paragraphs.idea: The future Redeemer will come from the house of Jesse, and the spirit of the Lord will grant him wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of God. He will judge justly, protect the poor, act through spiritual power, and draw his strength from righteousness and faithfulness.

paragraphs.paragraph: In the messianic world, peace and harmony will prevail among animals, and even children will be safe near creatures that were once dangerous. This transformation will result from the knowledge of the Lord filling the earth, while the Redeemer will stand as a signal toward which the nations turn.
paragraphs.title: Peace and Harmony in the World

answers: The wolf
The bear
The serpent
easy.explanation: Isaiah 11:6 says, “The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb.”
easy.q: Which animal will dwell with the lamb?

answers: Meat
Fish
Straw
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The lion shall eat straw like the ox.”
easy.q: What will the lion eat in the world described?

answers: The knowledge of the Lord
Riches
Wars
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “The earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord.”

answers: They will continue to devour one another
Peace and harmony will prevail among them
They will disappear from the earth
medium.explanation: The passage describes formerly dangerous and harmless animals living together peacefully.
medium.q: What is the central change in the relationships among the animals?

answers: Because the animals will sleep constantly
Because the children will stay far away
Because the animals will not hurt or destroy
medium.explanation: Isaiah says, “They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain.”
medium.q: Why will even children be safe near dangerous animals?

answers: A banner or signal raised for people to see
A source of water
A dwelling place
medium.explanation: An ensign is a visible sign or banner, and the Redeemer will stand as one for the peoples.
medium.q: What does the word “ensign” mean in this passage?

answers: The knowledge of the Lord is presented as the reason for the peaceful transformation
The passage says there is no connection
The knowledge of the Lord causes the animals to vanish
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the absence of hurt and destruction with the earth being full of the Lord’s knowledge.
challenge.q: What is the connection between peace among the animals and the earth being full of the knowledge of the Lord?

answers: An increase in violence
A profound change in the order and relationships of the world
A shortage of food
challenge.explanation: The lion’s changed diet illustrates the deep transformation described in the passage.
challenge.q: What does the lion eating straw like an ox symbolize?

answers: He will stand as an ensign toward which the Gentiles seek
He will hide from the nations
He will forbid the nations to approach
challenge.explanation: Isaiah 11:10 says the root of Jesse will stand “for an ensign of the people,” and the Gentiles will seek him.
challenge.q: What will be the role of the root of Jesse in relation to the nations?

paragraphs.idea: In the messianic world, peace and harmony will prevail among animals, and even children will be safe near creatures that were once dangerous. This transformation will result from the knowledge of the Lord filling the earth, while the Redeemer will stand as a signal toward which the nations turn.

paragraphs.paragraph: The Lord will gather the remnant of His people from distant lands, and the Redeemer will raise a banner recognized by the nations as a call to gather Israel. At the same time, the rivalry between Ephraim and Judah will disappear and friendship will prevail.
paragraphs.title: The Gathering of Israel and National Unity

answers: The remnant of His people
Only His enemies
Only the kings of the nations
easy.explanation: The Lord will recover and gather “the remnant of his people.”

answers: A sword
An ensign
A lampstand
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “He shall set up an ensign for the nations.”
easy.q: What will the Redeemer set up for the nations?

answers: Egypt and Assyria
Philistia and Edom
Ephraim and Judah
easy.explanation: Verse 13 specifically names Ephraim and Judah.
easy.q: Between whom will envy and rivalry disappear?

answers: To serve as a visible signal connected with the gathering of Israel
To announce the beginning of a drought
To separate Ephraim from Judah
medium.explanation: The ensign is associated with the nations and the assembling of Israel’s scattered people.
medium.q: What will be the purpose of the ensign set up for the nations?

answers: Ephraim will rule over Judah
Their envy and hostility will cease
Judah will abandon its people
medium.explanation: Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not vex Ephraim.
medium.q: What change will take place in the relationship between Ephraim and Judah?

answers: A raised banner or visible signal
A flowing spring
A private dwelling
medium.explanation: An ensign is a banner or sign raised so that people can recognize and follow it.
medium.q: In this context, what is an “ensign”?

answers: Both describe the restoration and bringing together of God’s people
They describe two unrelated nations
Unity prevents the gathering from happening
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the gathering of the scattered people with the healing of internal divisions.
challenge.q: How are the gathering of Israel and national unity related?

answers: The nations will recognize and respond to the sign associated with Israel’s restoration
The nations will conceal the ensign
The nations will prevent Israel from returning
challenge.explanation: The Gentiles seeking the ensign shows that the sign will be known beyond Israel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the Gentiles will seek the ensign?

answers: They will remain enemies but avoid open war
Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not vex Ephraim
Judah will completely eliminate Ephraim
challenge.explanation: This is the precise statement of Isaiah 11:13.
challenge.q: Which statement most accurately describes the restoration of relations between Ephraim and Judah?

paragraphs.idea: The Lord will gather the remnant of His people from distant lands, and the Redeemer will raise a banner recognized by the nations as a call to gather Israel. At the same time, the rivalry between Ephraim and Judah will disappear and friendship will prevail.

paragraphs.paragraph: Ephraim and Judah will act together against their enemies, and the Lord will make the rivers passable by drying and dividing them. A clear road will thus be opened for the remnant from Assyria and for the exiled Israelites to return, like the journey from Egypt.
paragraphs.title: Victory and the Road of Return

answers: Against their enemies
Against one another
Against the remnant of their people
easy.explanation: The passage describes them joining together against surrounding enemies.
easy.q: Against whom will Ephraim and Judah act together?

answers: Make it deeper
Strike it and divide it into streams
Cover it with clouds
easy.explanation: The Lord will smite the river “in the seven streams” and make people cross dryshod.
easy.q: What will the Lord do to the river?

answers: The remnant of the Lord’s people from Assyria
Only the kings of the nations
Only Israel’s enemies
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says there will be a highway for the remnant of His people from Assyria.
easy.q: For whom will the highway be provided?

answers: It will make the river possible to cross on dry ground
It will prevent the people from advancing
It will force the people to remain in exile
medium.explanation: The Lord will make people go over the river dryshod.
medium.q: How will the changing of the river help the returning people?

answers: Israel coming up out of Egypt
The conflict between Ephraim and Judah
The building of the temple
medium.explanation: The passage compares the return to Israel’s coming up from the land of Egypt.
medium.q: To which past event is the future return compared?

answers: A prepared road or route of travel
A military camp
A special garment
medium.explanation: Here, a highway is a clear and prepared route for the returning remnant.
medium.q: What does “highway” mean in this passage?

answers: Their cooperation enables them to act together against their enemies
Their unity causes them to separate
The victory occurs only after they return to rivalry
challenge.explanation: Their shared action against their enemies demonstrates the strength of their restored unity.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the unity of Ephraim and Judah and the victory described?

answers: It will be a divinely enabled deliverance and leading of the people
The people will remain in Egypt
The return has no connection with Israel’s past
challenge.explanation: The comparison presents the future return as another great act of God’s deliverance.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with the Exodus emphasize about the future return?

answers: Enemies, division, exile, and blocked roads
Cooperation, changed waters, an open highway, and return
War, famine, construction, and abandonment
challenge.explanation: The verses move from united action to a miraculous crossing, a prepared road, and the return of the remnant.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the ideas in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: Ephraim and Judah will act together against their enemies, and the Lord will make the rivers passable by drying and dividing them. A clear road will thus be opened for the remnant from Assyria and for the exiled Israelites to return, like the journey from Egypt.
